known_limitations: S4B intentionally supplies no authority-bearing concrete provider; the default entrypoint is fail-closed until final Stage-4 integration.

Authority adoption, fencing-token mechanics, persistent-root ownership, legacy-retirement policy, and orchestration semantics are outside S4B and must be wired from independently qualified providers during final integration.

The repository connector exposes no remote shell or workflow-dispatch action, so pytest was executed in a local equivalent checkout rather than on the private GitHub working tree. GitHub API comparisons independently verified ancestry, touched paths, and Semantic Freeze blob identity.
The optional full-repository static authority command was not feasible without an executable full private-repository checkout.
integration_notes: Final integration must instantiate CanonicalRuntimeControllerR11 with concrete AuthorityAdoptionProvider, PersistentStateRootProvider, LegacyRetirementGuard, RecoveryProvider, AuthorityLeaseProvider, and OrchestrationProvider implementations.
Do not replace build_fail_closed_runtime with a legacy fallback. Production wiring must be explicit and must preserve provider failures as fail-closed startup failures.
AuthorityLeaseProvider fencing tokens remain opaque to S4B; final writer integration must enforce the separately qualified fencing contract at authoritative mutation sites.
RecoveryProvider must return exactly the adopted authority_id and generation; S4B rejects any recovery-created generation.

OrchestrationProvider.seal_runtime_state is treated only as a shutdown identity observation; it may not be used by S4B to decide scientific truth, create evidence, advance generation, or rewrite history.
Stage-2/Stage-3 qualification harnesses remain qualification/engineering surfaces and must not be adopted as production authority merely through Python call reachability.
